# Supporting Testimony

Testimony is open-source research: a Lean 4 library that formalises Christian
arguments from Scripture with every premise sourced, classified, and open to
challenge.

## What funding buys

Rigour and review time — not conclusions.

- **Expert review honoraria.** Biblical scholars and Lean engineers paid to
  find errors in the encodings. This is the project's single biggest
  constraint: a subtly wrong formalisation is worse than none, and only a
  qualified human reader can catch one.
- **Compute** for autoformalisation experiments across the corpus.
- **Conference travel** to present the work and recruit reviewers — SBL for
  the biblical-studies side, Lean Together for the formal-methods side.
- **Infrastructure.** Domain and hosting.

## What funding does not buy

No supporter, at any level, influences what the library concludes.

Rival interpretations are encoded on their merits and cited to their own
sources. A result that contradicts the maintainers' theological position — or
a donor's — is a result the project keeps and publishes. The
[scope and limits](https://testimonyproject.info/scope-and-limits.html) page
sets out what a proof assistant can and cannot establish here; funding changes
none of it.

If that constraint makes a prospective supporter uncomfortable, the project
would rather forgo the support than soften the constraint.

## Supporters

Named supporters are listed in [SUPPORTERS.md](../SUPPORTERS.md), by consent.
